title: Evidence Signal Normalizer V2 for AI Runner Selection
goal: Improve AI runner selection by converting raw tool output into richer, typed evidence signals that describe technology, routes, parameters, auth state, data flows, and test context.
scope: Evidence graph/signal normalization, runner capability matching, AI-loop next-action selection, and tests for signal-to-runner decisions.
generation_reason: The codebase already has signal scoring and AI runner selection, but discovering more vulnerabilities requires better normalized evidence signals so AI chooses targeted follow-up tests instead of broad batteries.

review_findings: AI-first vulnerability discovery depends on evidence-to-hypothesis quality.
Signals should include context such as JWT, upload, GraphQL, forms, object IDs, roles, auth-only routes, and parameter locations.
Runner choice must remain deterministic and evidence-backed.

inputs.prerequisite_backlog: REQUIRES: backlog-352 AI-driven signal scoring and existing evidence graph normalizer

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement until this package is the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Improve signal normalization and planner decisions only. Do not add new scanner capabilities or change runner execution semantics.
constraints.deterministic_planning: AI-facing signals and next-action choices must be reproducible from stored evidence.

success_criteria: Evidence normalizer emits typed signals for route, method, parameter location, auth requirement, role context, object identifier, upload surface, token/JWT, GraphQL, redirect, and reflected/stored context where evidence exists.
Runner selection uses richer signals to prefer targeted tests and document blockers for irrelevant tests.
AI-loop next-action records include explicit signal refs that justify why a runner was selected or skipped.
Tests prove a small fixture evidence graph selects targeted runners instead of a broad generic queue.
Signal output remains redacted and evidence-first.

acceptance_criteria: Planner tests show evidence-backed runner selection improves from raw tool names to typed signals.
Skipped runners include blocker reasons tied to missing signals.
No new runtime execution path, approval bypass, or credential materialization is introduced.

before_promotion: NEXT_TASK.md must contain this task as the single active task.
after_completion: Promote the next true open task into NEXT_TASK.md, or record that no active backlog task remains in NEXT_TASK.md.

out_of_scope: Changing runner risk tiers or approval requirements.
